issues.body: The malformed-object table exercises an invalid `body`, but never an invalid `title` with an otherwise valid positive issue number and null/absent body. Consequently, changing the guard's key tuple from `("title", "body")` to `("body",)` would leave the added suite green. That survivor matters because a malformed title can hide a legacy title-only alert and, if accepted, allow the failure path to create a duplicate instead of refusing the incomplete dedupe view. The implementation is sound; this is a focused regression-coverage gap rather than a current production defect.
issues.fix_hint: Add a wrapped full-`main()` case such as `[{"number": 7, "title": 42, "body": null}]` on a failing tick, asserting rc 0, a sanitized warning, no payload echo, and no mutation after `issue list`. Verify that removing only `title` from `_usable_row`'s checked keys makes this row fail.
issues.title: The title-type half of the row guard lacks an independent red test

verdict.summary: The prior major finding is resolved. `_usable_row` validates every value consumed by the matcher and every issue number passed to mutation commands, explicitly excluding booleans and non-positive integers. `_find_open_alert` refuses the complete listing before matching, so malformed or partial evidence produces a sanitized soft skip with no create, edit, comment, or close. The new full-`main()` cases cover the previously demonstrated crashes and unsafe mutation targets in both watchdog modes, and the null-body case prevents an over-strict guard from disabling real listings. One minor mutation-testing gap remains: no case independently proves that the `title` half of the title/body type guard is necessary.
